items.title: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach
items.summary:
Hackers breached the US Air Force’s Cloud One platform, adding to recent federal attacks on agencies such as the FBI, CIA, and Treasury Department.
The breach highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in government cloud services.

items.title: Your Firewall Isn't Enough: The Hidden Risk of Unmanaged VMs
items.summary:
Unmanaged virtual machines, unpatched servers, and excessive permissions create security blind spots.
Centralized infrastructure management, strict access controls, and automated lifecycle processes can mitigate these risks.

items.title: Malwarebytes Antivirus: Get 50% off during Black Friday 2026
items.summary:
Malwarebytes is offering a 50% discount on security subscriptions for individuals, families, and small businesses during its Black Friday 2026 sale.
The promotion includes antivirus, VPN, identity theft protection, and data removal services.

items.title: Japan’s education ministry discloses breach of government procurement system
items.summary:
Hackers accessed Japan’s education ministry procurement system, potentially exposing business records and email addresses.
The breach was disclosed earlier this week.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: FIFA hacked, cybercriminals claim access to sensitive internal records
items.summary:
Cybercriminals gained access to limited personal and business information within FIFA’s systems.
FIFA is cooperating with law enforcement to investigate the incident.

items.title: Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach
items.summary:
SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident after reports that hackers infiltrated its software development infrastructure and may have accessed source code.
The company is reviewing its security posture.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control
items.summary:
Researchers discovered a Microsoft Store application that delivered the Vinci remote access trojan via a fake snipping tool installer.
The attack began with a redirect to a malicious site hosting the installer.

items.title: Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028
items.summary:
Microsoft will remove the Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) server role from the upcoming Windows Server 2028 release.
Users will need to adopt alternative update management solutions.

items.title: UK Welfare and Pension Services Taken Offline Following Cyber Incident
items.summary:
The UK Department for Work and Pensions took its online services offline following a cyber incident.
Regular pension and benefit payments were not affected.

items.title: In Other News: Tanker Cyberattacks, EU Quantum Act, New VirusTotal Capabilities
items.summary: SecurityWeek reports on tanker cyberattacks, the EU Quantum Act, and new VirusTotal capabilities, along with other notable cybersecurity stories.

items.title: FIFA Confirms Cyber-Attack, Personal and Business Information Compromised
items.summary: FIFA confirmed a cyber‑attack that exposed limited personal and business information. The breach involved unauthorized data access and is under investigation.

items.title: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks
items.summary: Drupal has warned of a new site takeover vulnerability that attackers are exploiting. The flaw allows breach and hijacking of unpatched websites; users should apply patches immediately.

items.title: British social security system techies yank services offline following 'cyber incident'
items.summary: UK social security services were taken offline following a cyber incident. Pensioners were assured that their funds will be paid normally while the incident is investigated.

items.title: SAP confirms security incident after suspicious GitHub activity
items.summary: SAP confirmed a security incident after detecting suspicious GitHub activity. The company took urgent action to protect customers and is continuing its investigation.

items.title: Flight Centre Travel Group warns of customer data breach involving some passport details
items.summary: Flight Centre Travel Group disclosed a customer data breach affecting some passport details. Travelers who booked accommodation may have had names and passport information accessed; investigation is ongoing.

items.title: 100,000 Potentially Impacted by Colorado Data Breach
items.summary: Hackers breached the myColorado digital ID application, accessing user‑uploaded data. Approximately 100,000 users may be impacted by the breach.

items.title: Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware
items.summary: A supply‑chain attack tampered with Q‑Dir and DesktopOK installers on SoftwareOK, delivering remote‑access malware. The attack affected both new downloads and updates; users should verify integrity.

items.title: Microsoft pushes emergency hotpatch to fix Windows Server crashes
items.summary: Microsoft released an emergency hotpatch for Windows Server 2025 to fix crashes caused by the KB5131077 security update. The patch addresses stability issues and should be applied promptly.

items.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
items.summary: A 12‑year‑old Linux kernel NFS vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑99362) can give remote attackers root privileges. The flaw remains critical and systems should be patched.

items.title: Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach
items.summary: A vulnerability in hex.pm allowed attackers to run commands on web servers. No data modification was detected, but database reads were unlogged; users should review security.

items.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack, Source Code Reportedly Compromised
items.summary: SAP confirmed a cyberattack. Hackers used stolen employee tokens on GitHub to copy and alter source code.

items.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
items.summary: A zero‑day vulnerability in Cacti enables remote code execution via four unauthenticated HTTP requests. The proof‑of‑concept is tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT.

items.title: US seizes nearly $17 billion in global war on scam rings
items.summary: The U.S. DOJ seized nearly $17 billion in its largest crackdown on scam rings, targeting over 800 alleged scammers across 85 federal districts. The operation included new charges, convictions, and extraditions.

items.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
items.summary: Free e-government platform serving two billion people in ten countries has a critical SQL injection vulnerability that could leak data. The vulnerability is in India's Digital Infrastructure for Governance Impact and Transformation tool.

items.title: Cyberattack disrupts global news distribution platform at France’s AFP
items.summary: AFP’s global news distribution platform was taken offline after a cyberattack, disrupting content delivery to media organizations worldwide.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: British government takes services offline following ‘cyber incident’
items.summary: The UK Department for Work and Pensions experienced a cyber incident, leading to the temporary shutdown of several services as a precaution.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: OpenAI warns GPT-6.2 Astra will hit usage limits 40% faster because it fixed a bug
items.summary: OpenAI has fixed a bug that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 usage, causing users to hit usage limits 40% faster. The change was announced to improve accuracy of usage tracking.

items.title: NordVPN Black Friday Deal: Get 78% off VPN plans in 2026
items.summary: NordVPN is offering a 78% discount on VPN plans for 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday, plus three extra months of protection. The promotion is available for new and existing subscribers.

items.title: Fake paid expert interviews impersonate brands to steal Google logins
items.summary: A phishing campaign called GoodGuys impersonates major brands to steal Google and Okta credentials via fake paid expert interview invitations. Targets include Google, Nvidia, Accenture, and SpaceX.

items.title: FIFA Says It Has Been Victim of a Cyberattack Accessing ‘Personal and Business Information’
items.summary: FIFA confirmed it was a victim of a cyberattack that accessed personal and business information, though details remain undisclosed. The organization has not specified the timing or scope of the breach.

items.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
items.summary: UK privacy watchdog under independent review for workplace culture. Focus on leadership, accountability, and staff concern handling. Former commissioner John Edwards resigned.

items.title: 'Significant number of customer records' pwned in Flight Centre Travel Group breach
items.summary: Flight Centre Travel Group suffered a breach compromising a significant number of customer records. Attack part of ongoing global booking system incidents.

items.title: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension
items.summary: Remus infostealer uses a malicious Chrome extension to steal Gmail messages. Operators marketed it as a zero‑day exploit in Google’s email service.

items.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
items.summary: PolinRider campaign planted a Python loader in GitHub repositories to spread malware. Activity traced back to February 2025.

items.title: CISA Issues Alert After Danfoss Reveals Critical Flaw in Fridge Controllers
items.summary: CISA issued an alert after Danfoss discovered a critical flaw in fridge controllers. Food retailers are at risk.

items.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
items.summary: Peninsula Energy’s Wyoming uranium plant shut down after a cyberattack. Control systems were affected; no restart date announced.

items.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
items.summary: Company exposed backups by placing the backup server in the same Windows domain as production, highlighting the need to segregate backup infrastructure.

items.title: Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: CVE-2026-103406 in Juniper Session Smart Conductor allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. The flaw has been exploited in recent attacks.

items.title: Preinstalled Keenadu malware turns up on 220,000+ Android devices
items.summary: Kaspersky identified over 220,000 Android devices shipped with Keenadu malware preinstalled. Device infections grew 2.5× in the past year.

items.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
items.summary: SYS010 infostealer delivered via Meta ads enrolls browsers into enterprise management, forcing an extension that steals Gmail and Outlook emails.

items.title: Hackers help themselves to 1Password's source code and customer data
items.summary: 1Password suffered a breach where attackers accessed source code and customer data through malicious code in backend services. The company confirmed that user passwords remain secure.

items.title: Most Wanted: The Phishing Kits and Techniques Getting Past Security Controls
items.summary: A study highlights phishing kits that successfully bypass email security, web filtering, and safe browsing, measuring their breakthrough rate to inform security teams.

items.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
items.summary: 1Password disclosed unauthorized access to backend systems that led to the theft of customer data and source code, while vaults were not compromised.

items.title: Home Office Reprimanded After GDPR Failure at the Border
items.summary: The ICO reprimanded the UK Home Office for GDPR failures that caused distress at the border due to data integrity issues.

items.title: Data recovery firm co-founder accused of cashing in on ransomware victims
items.summary: A co‑founder of a Florida data recovery firm was indicted for paying ransomware gangs while claiming no involvement, facing wire fraud charges.

items.title: 1Password Hit by Backend Breach via Hijacked Employee GitHub Account
items.summary: Attackers used a hijacked 1Password employee GitHub account to access customer data, but did not reach user vaults.

items.title: UK Home Office waved through border system without a working fix for bad data
items.summary: The ICO reprimand followed the Home Office’s failure to correct bad data, risking wrongful detention; a temporary fix took over a year to implement.

items.title: Drupal Installer Patch Left a Gap Attackers Are Already Exploiting
items.summary: Drupal warned that a previous installer patch left a vulnerability that attackers are exploiting to take over websites.

items.title: 1Password breached through hijacked employee GitHub account, customer names and emails stolen
items.summary: 1Password disclosed a breach via a hijacked employee GitHub account that resulted in stolen customer names, emails, and source code; vaults remained untouched.

items.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
items.summary: A hacker used a compromised employee GitHub account to push malicious code and steal customer records, but 1Password vaults were not accessed.

items.title: Cyprus Becomes Espionage Target for Iranian Hackers
items.summary: Iranian threat group Volant Manticore is targeting Cypriot organizations for intelligence gathering. The group was previously undocumented. The attacks focus on gathering information for Tehran.

items.title: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
items.summary: Drupal core has a highly critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-136716) that is actively exploited. The flaw involves improper condition checks. It is related to CVE-2026-132165, addressing remaining vulnerable installation states.

items.title: Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
items.summary: CISA added 10 known exploited vulnerabilities to its catalog, including five affecting Mitel MiCollab. The listed CVE-2026-133275 allows arbitrary file upload. Other vendors impacted include Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss.

items.title: Black Friday cybersecurity deals 2026: Stay safe, spend less
items.summary: Security vendors are offering Black Friday 2026 discounts on cybersecurity tools. The article lists deals and advises reviewing fine print. It highlights opportunities to purchase security solutions at lower prices.

items.title: Proxmox 9.3 adds production snapshots for SAN-backed VMs
items.summary: Proxmox VE 9.3 introduces production snapshot support for VMs on shared LVM storage over iSCSI and Fibre Channel SANs. Each guest receives a persistent identity across migration, backup, and restore. The feature is intended for production use.

items.title: More than 4,400 malicious domains are waiting for holiday shoppers
items.summary: FortiGuard Labs identified over 24,000 new domains with holiday shopping keywords, 4,400 of which are malicious. Cybercriminals plan to exploit shoppers with fraudulent storefronts, impersonation, payment fraud, and account takeover attacks.

items.title: People are willing to pay to vanish from search results
items.summary: A survey found that 55% of U.S. adults would pay to remove personal information from public search results. 53% want a record of all searches for their name over the past five years. The study highlights privacy concerns.

items.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Turn Fake .NET Job Assessments Into Malware Delivery Traps
items.summary: Researchers discovered 13 malicious NuGet packages that masquerade as fake .NET job assessment tools. The packages deliver malware when built or run. They target Windows .NET developers with WinUI 3 and WPF controls.

items.title: Smashing Security podcast #494: The Russian accused of spying on Palantir from Starbucks
items.summary: Podcast discusses a Russian spy recruited via Telegram for $15,000 to surveil Palantir, using a cover story of asking a woman out. It also examines a think tank with 300 experts, including Henry Kissinger, and its audience.

items.title: UK’s long-awaited National Cyber Action Plan delayed until December
items.summary: The UK government has delayed the release of its National Cyber Action Plan to December 9, after originally planning a mid‑November publication. The plan outlines defenses against state‑backed and criminal hackers.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks
items.summary: Threat actors chain PHP2Shell and Fragnesia exploits to target Palo Alto Networks devices with internet‑exposed management interfaces. Palo Alto warns of ongoing attacks.

items.title: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
items.summary: 1Password disclosed a breach after an employee’s GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to backend services, resulting in customer data theft.

items.title: FIFA says hackers accessed ‘limited set of personal and business information’
items.summary: FIFA reports that hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information. The organization is working with authorities to investigate the breach.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
items.summary: A study shows U.S. water systems are more vulnerable than previously thought, with attackers able to breach systems without exploiting software bugs.

items.title: Oh, is it Thanksgiving? I hadn’t noticed!
items.summary: Author thanks the cybersecurity community for their support and offers remarks on threat actors, noting the timing of the Thanksgiving holiday.

items.title: Rapid7 Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Integrated Security Operations Center Systems
items.summary: Rapid7 has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Integrated SOC Systems, recognized for its completeness of vision and execution.

items.title: Florida ransomware recovery CEO indicted for allegedly paying hacker ransoms
items.summary: The CEO of a ransomware recovery firm was indicted for lying about services and for paying ransoms to cybercriminals.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Australia passes tough legislation requiring big tech to preempt foreseeable harms
items.summary: Australia’s Digital Duty of Care Act requires large tech companies to establish protocols that protect users from violence, rape, and other significant harms.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft's NTLM security changes trip up third-party logins
items.summary: Microsoft’s recent NTLM security changes have caused compatibility issues for third‑party login implementations.

items.title: US Treasury financial crimes unit becomes latest fed breach victim
items.summary:
FinCEN, part of the US Treasury, experienced a breach.
The agency took systems offline, extended filing deadlines, and is investigating unauthorized access.

items.title: CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers
items.summary:
CISA has warned of a critical vulnerability in Danfoss AK‑SM 8xxA Series refrigeration controllers.
These controllers are used in commercial refrigeration, HVAC, and lighting systems.

items.title: US Anti-Scam Surge Hits 800 Defendants and 29 Scam Compounds
items.summary:
The DOJ anti‑scam surge has targeted over 800 defendants.
The FBI has identified more than 29 scam compounds.

items.title: Attackers Target .NET Developers With Poisoned Job Assessments
items.summary:
Attackers released 13 malicious NuGet packages in a fake recruitment campaign.
The malware targets .NET developers.

items.title: Two Newly Disclosed GeoServer Vulnerabilities Under Attack
items.summary:
Attackers are probing GeoServer instances for two high‑severity vulnerabilities.
These can be chained for unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.title: It's a Bot World. We're Just Living in It
items.summary:
Bot detection is increasingly ineffective.
Security teams should limit privileged access for both humans and bots equally.

items.title: InfraTrust warns of exploited supply chain flaws in network appliances
items.summary:
InfraTrust reports that most recent infrastructure security advisories involve third‑party software flaws in network appliances.
These flaws are in bundled third‑party code rather than vendor code.

items.title: Palo Alto Fixes Fragnesia Kernel Bug Chained With PHP2Shell in Firewall Attacks
items.summary:
Palo Alto Networks patched the Fragnesia kernel bug.
Attackers had chained it with PHP2Shell to compromise firewalls.

items.title: Shufti Fraud Hub exposes suspicious links between seemingly legitimate accounts
items.summary:
Shufti launched Fraud Hub, a fraud intelligence layer.
It connects identity, device, biometric, and behavioral signals to detect coordinated fraud networks.

items.title: ShinyHunters Claims Comeback, New Inception Group Rejects Alleged Ties
items.summary:
An account linked to ShinyHunters announced the group’s return.
Okta identified possible connections between Inception and ShinyHunters, but the new Inception group denies ties.

items.title: Latin America Sees Cyberattacks on Ports, Pipelines & Manufacturing
items.summary: Cyberattacks are increasingly targeting industrial systems across Latin America, including ports, pipelines, and manufacturing. Recent incidents involve the Port of Santos in Brazil and an Argentine pipeline, underscoring the region's growing infrastructure vulnerability.

items.title: US Treasury’s FinCEN Disconnects Systems Following Cyber Incident
items.summary: FinCEN has taken some systems offline after a cybersecurity incident and extended filing deadlines for affected users. The agency is investigating the disruption while maintaining the portal's operational status.

items.title: Critical Drupal installer flaw under active attack (CVE-2026-132165)
items.summary: CVE-2026-132165 allows attackers to take over unpatched Drupal sites without authentication. The vulnerability has been actively exploited since November 19 and affects sites used by governments, universities, and enterprises.

items.title: Ground Truth: CISO Matt Martin on Building a Real Security Program Without an Enterprise Budget
items.summary: CISO Matt Martin of Western Carolina University discusses establishing a security program with limited resources. He emphasizes practical strategies for building effective security without a large enterprise budget.

items.title: Suspected ransomware attack disrupts cancer treatments, surgeries at Guadeloupe hospital
items.summary: A suspected ransomware attack on the University Hospital of Guadeloupe forced doctors to postpone surgeries and suspend some cancer treatments. The incident caused a return to paper records while the national cybersecurity agency investigates.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: FinCEN investigates cybersecurity incident, takes systems offline
items.summary: FinCEN has taken systems offline after a cybersecurity incident and is extending filing deadlines for affected users. The filing portal remains operational while the agency investigates the breach.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Two GeoServer Flaws as Researchers Warn of Unauthenticated RCE Chains
items.summary: Threat actors are exploiting two patched GeoServer vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, which allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaws enable arbitrary file reads and potential code execution on affected servers.

items.title: U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Agency Takes Some Systems Offline After Cyber Intrusion
items.summary: FinCEN reported unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems and has taken some systems offline as a precaution. The agency continues to collect suspicious activity reports and other BSA filings.

items.title: CVE-2026-123903: Critical VMware Directory Service Authentication Bypass affects vCenter
items.summary: CVE-2026-123903 is a critical authentication bypass in VMware Directory Service that can allow attackers to gain unauthorized access to vCenter. The vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 9.8, was addressed in Broadcom's November 24 advisory.

items.title: Credential Remediation Is Slow When You Don’t Know What Will Break
items.summary: GitGuardian's State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 found that over 64% of valid secrets from 2022 remained active in 2026, indicating slow remediation. The study suggests prioritizing credential revocation by impact rather than validity alone.

items.title: US Treasury Investigates Cyber Incident Amid Reported Federal Agency Breaches
items.summary: The Treasury’s Crimes Enforcement Network is investigating a cyber incident that caused some federal agency services to be taken offline.

items.title: Drupal Fail2Install Exploit Details Emerge as Critical RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation
items.summary: CISA has added the Drupal core vulnerability CVE-2026-132165 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, requiring federal agencies to patch it by November 27, 2026. The flaw allows remote code execution with a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: Bots exploited leaked AWS key from Docker image in under 8 seconds
items.summary: Researchers discovered that bots can locate and use a leaked AWS access key embedded in a Docker image in under eight seconds, exposing the risk of publishing credentials in container registries.

items.title: Microsoft fixes Microsoft 365 bug blocking access to Office apps
items.summary: Microsoft has resolved a bug that prevented certain Microsoft 365 customers from accessing Office applications, restoring normal service.

items.title: Gatwick drop-off customers' personal data exposed in supplier breach
items.summary: A supplier breach exposed Gatwick Airport drop‑off customers’ AutoPay login credentials, vehicle records, and limited payment and customer service email information.

items.title: The Great Escape: Tradecraft insights from an agentic swarm
items.summary: A blog analyzes the tradecraft of an OpenAI‑linked agentic swarm that operated in 2026, comparing its traceable activity to early signals of agentic attacks seen in the wild.

items.title: Securing Grandma's groceries with Pierre Cadieux
items.summary: Pierre Cadieux recounts how his early help‑desk work in the 1990s, correlating Windows and Unix logs, sparked his interest in cybersecurity.

items.title: Ransomware Attacks Surge 23% in October Following Record Quarter
items.summary: NCC Group researchers note a 23% increase in ransomware attacks in October, indicating a shift in the cyber threat landscape.

items.title: Plagiarism Checker Turnitin Investigating Cyberattack
items.summary: Turnitin reports that its systems remain fully operational and secure while it investigates a cyberattack on its plagiarism‑checking platform.

items.title: Hackers now exploit critical Drupal RCE flaw to hijack sites
items.summary: The Drupal security team confirms that the critical RCE vulnerability CVE-2026-132165 has been actively exploited to hijack unpatched sites since at least Thursday.

items.title: NCSC Shares Guidance to Tackle Agentic Threat From ARTEX-Like Tools
items.summary: UK National Cyber Security Centre urges strong operational discipline to manage agentic offensive frameworks similar to ARTEX.

items.title: UK Authorized Push Payment Losses Surge 22% as Fraudsters Steal £660m
items.summary: Authorized push payment fraud rose 22% in the first half of the year, with fraudsters stealing £660 million.

items.title: Hackers Exploited CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm RCE Flaw to Compromise 6 Package Registry Servers
items.summary: Hackers ran operating‑system commands on six Hex.pm production servers using a CVSS 10.0 RCE flaw that existed since February 2016; the service patched all servers within 15 minutes of the first request.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑131914 in the abandoned Idunno AntiCsrf library allows remote code execution via a single crafted web request.

items.title: Microsoft confirms authentication issues after November updates
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that addressed a high‑severity remote code execution vulnerability.

items.title: How to protect against preinstalled Android malware
items.summary: An article outlines Trojans embedded in Android firmware, provides statistics, discusses risks to corporate users, and recommends countermeasures with Kaspersky Next.

items.title: Police disrupt 57 illegal IPTV services and trace €26 million in crypto
items.summary: Europol coordinated a five‑day operation that disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services, identified 321 pirate sites, and traced more than €26 million in cryptocurrency.

items.title: Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: CISA added a Drupal core remote code execution vulnerability to its KEV catalog and instructed federal agencies to patch it within three days.

items.title: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system
items.summary: Unknown attackers reportedly breached an open‑source intelligence analysis system at the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency.

items.title: Exploited: Abandoned Idunno.AntiCsrf library opens legacy ASP.NET apps to RCE (CVE-2026-131914)
items.summary: US‑CISA added CVE‑2026‑131914, an RCE vulnerability in the abandoned Idunno.AntiCsrf library, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

items.title: Com-Affiliated Hackers Hijack Cloud Accounts via Vishing for Data Theft and Extortion
items.summary:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 reports ongoing vishing attacks by Com‑affiliated threat actors since August 2026.
Targets include financial, healthcare, legal, and construction sectors in the U.S., U.K., and Australia.
Attacks have resulted in data theft and extortion attempts.

items.title: Credential harvesting goes from fringe activity to major exploitation trend
items.summary:
Credential harvesting accounted for 13% of all vulnerability exploitation from Jan‑Nov 2026, rising from 1% in January to 25‑35% in September‑October.
694 CVEs were exploited, with 127 (18%) used for database attacks.

items.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
items.summary:
WordPress removed six WP Connect plugins after backdooring on Nov 22, 2026, which allowed arbitrary code execution on sites with the plugins.
The removal prevented the malicious releases from going live.

items.title: Security+ builds the foundation. SSCP proves you can execute
items.summary:
The article discusses the importance of both cybersecurity knowledge and operational readiness.
It emphasizes that professionals must move beyond theoretical foundations to demonstrate practical execution in high‑stakes scenarios.

items.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week
items.summary:
VMware released a third critical patch bundle in a week, addressing four new critical vulnerabilities, including an unauthorized access flaw in vCenter.
The updates aim to mitigate risks that could disrupt services during the holiday period.

items.title: Holiday scam losses force some victims to cut back on essentials
items.summary:
McAfee research shows holiday shopping scam victimization rose from 22% in 2025 to 42% in 2026.
Confidence in detecting scams fell, and many Americans report financial losses that force them to cut back on essentials.
